name: SysML v2 Target Notation for Turing Generator MVP
purpose: Defines the deliberately limited SysML v2 textual notation subset that the Turing Generator MVP is allowed to generate.
scope_principle: The MVP reduces scope by limiting the generated SysML v2 language subset, not by accepting invalid syntax.

target_notation_status.extension_policy: Any additional SysML v2 construct must be explicitly added to this target notation file before it may be generated by the MVP.

allowed_constructs.name: Package
usage_rules: Use packages for top-level and nested model organization.
Use clear package names that reflect the model area.
Avoid deeply nested package structures in MVP output unless required.

allowed_constructs.name: Documentation block
allowed_constructs.purpose: Capture human-readable rationale, traceability, assumptions and review notes.
usage_rules: Use doc blocks for rationale and traceability where formal cross-file references are intentionally avoided.
Use doc blocks to preserve source references, recipe IDs, agent personality IDs and human decision IDs.
Do not use documentation blocks as a substitute for validation.
allowed_constructs.example: doc /* This element was generated from approved model data. */

allowed_constructs.name: Part definition
usage_rules: Use part definitions for logical or physical components.
Use singular, descriptive names.
Avoid implementation-specific file or class names in logical model output.

allowed_constructs.name: Part usage
allowed_constructs.purpose: Instantiate or use a component definition within a specific architecture configuration.
usage_rules: Use part usages to represent concrete architecture configurations.
Use lower camel case for usage names.
Use qualified names when referencing definitions from another package.

allowed_constructs.name: Action definition
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define reusable system functions or workflow capabilities.
usage_rules: Use action definitions for system-level functions.
Use verb-object names such as IngestLegacyData or GenerateSysMLv2Artifacts.
Do not model Python functions as action definitions on system level.

allowed_constructs.name: Action usage
allowed_constructs.purpose: Use a defined action as a workflow step or included function.
usage_rules: Use action usages to show included functions in workflow or detailed views.
Use lower camel case for usage names.
Detailed execution order may be described in doc blocks when formal control flow is not required.

allowed_constructs.name: Requirement definition
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define reusable requirement categories in manually curated architecture model files.
usage_rules: Use requirement definitions for requirement categories.
Use this construct primarily in architecture model files.
Generated model output may use a smaller requirement subset.

allowed_constructs.name: Requirement usage
usage_rules: Use requirement usages for explicitly modeled requirements.
Use stable IDs where requirements are part of the architecture model.
Generated MVP output shall only create requirements if the selected recipe explicitly requests requirement generation.

allowed_constructs.name: Simple specialization
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define more specific element types from a base type.
usage_rules: Use only simple one-level specialization in generated MVP output.
Avoid complex inheritance hierarchies.
Use specialization only when it improves model clarity.

allowed_constructs.name: Qualified reference
usage_rules: Use qualified references when definitions are stored in a separate package.
Keep package names stable.
Validate quoted package names in the selected SysML v2 environment before relying on them for generated output.

allowed_constructs.name: Item definition
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define relevant data or artifact types exchanged in the workflow.
usage_rules: Use item definitions for important data or artifact concepts.
Use item definitions for model-level concepts, not for every physical file.
Keep item definitions stable and reviewable.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced ports and interfaces
restricted_constructs.reason: Interface and port modeling is outside the initial MVP target notation.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Do not generate unless explicitly added to the target notation after validation.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced item flows
restricted_constructs.reason: Formal item flow modeling is not required for the first MVP.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Represent artifact flow in doc blocks or JSON traceability records for the MVP.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced constraint modeling
restricted_constructs.reason: Formal constraint modeling is beyond the initial MVP scope.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Use requirement or doc-based constraints in the MVP unless formal constraints are explicitly introduced later.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced verification modeling
restricted_constructs.reason: The MVP prepares validation artifacts but does not generate a full verification model.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Store validation findings as reviewable artifacts instead.

restricted_constructs.name: Complex behavioral control flow
restricted_constructs.reason: The MVP uses textual workflow descriptions in doc blocks rather than full formal execution semantics.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Use action definitions and action usages with doc-based flow descriptions.

restricted_constructs.name: Deep cross-file formal references
restricted_constructs.reason: Cross-file references may be fragile in the MVP toolchain.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Prefer doc-based traceability or validated qualified references.

packages.style: PascalCase or numbered package names when mirroring architecture model structure

required_doc_content_for_generated_eleme: source or input reference where applicable
doc_block_style: Use stable IDs for findings, decisions and traceability where possible.
Avoid embedding large raw input text in doc blocks.
Store large source content in separate artifacts and reference it.

mvp_generation_profiles.description: Generate a SysML v2 package containing action definitions, action usages and doc-based workflow descriptions.
Generate a SysML v2 package containing logical component definitions, usages and doc-based allocation notes.
Generate a SysML v2 package containing requirement definitions and requirement usages when explicitly requested.

validation_policy.validation_environment: Selected SysML v2 validation environment, initially SysIDE where applicable.
validation_policy.validation_rule: Generated SysML v2 artifacts shall be prepared for validation. Validation findings shall be stored as reviewable artifacts and shall not silently modify generated output.

extension_policy.rule: Do not generate constructs outside the allowed target notation unless this file is intentionally updated.
extension_steps: Identify required new SysML v2 construct.
Add construct to allowed_constructs or restricted_constructs.
Update recipes that may use the construct.
